law: A telemetry hypothesis is accepted only with matched causal evidence, not one screen sample; diagnostics are not primary timing.

H1_load_parse_contention.statement: Pool-efficiency loss is caused by contention inside the workers' load/parse phase (co-tenant-independent).
reasoning: If per-row run wall were roughly flat across W while application wall scaled, in-run contention would be refuted as the dominant efficiency loss; growth >25% (the P00 same-config spread) would support it.
caveats: coarse span: decode/topology/trace/metrics are inside 'run'; a refutation applies to the whole span, not the load/parse slice (P02 hooks required to separate)
single matrix pass per W; co-tenant noise law (P00: 25-28% same-config spread) applies to absolute walls

H2_commit_backpressure.statement: Worker result_put blocks behind the coordinator's commit owning the only reader (residual backpressure motivating P04 drain).

evidence.alignment_note: design 01: result_put durations live in the streamed workerpool jsonl, never in the events riding the result they measure

reasoning: max result_put=11.832585s over 32 puts; coordinator commit wall sum=4.620062s over 32 commits
Synchronous-channel law: a put returns once the result reaches the pipe; puts lasting microseconds next to hundred-ms commits refute backpressure at this scale.
H2_commit_backpressure.consequence: refuted_at_this_scale means the P04 bounded independent drain has no demonstrated residual to cover and stays conditional (P04 runs ONLY if residual backpressure is measured, per the /goal order).

H3_replay_contention.statement: Trace replay contends on memory bandwidth / thread pools across W/T configurations.
reasoning: The compiled outer replay does not exist yet (P03C scope); no replay-phase span is separable in this matrix.
Required experiments (design 01) remain: W1T4 vs W2T2 vs W4T1 with active thread counts, and Python-loop vs compiled driver at IDENTICAL configuration.
